lawRefs: Minn. Stat. 290.06 subd. 2c and 2d (rates, indexed brackets)
Minn. Stat. 290.0123 (standard deduction, additional amount for aged/blind, high-income limitation)
Minn. Stat. 290.0132 subd. 26 (Social Security subtraction) and subd. 34 (public pension subtraction)
header.notes: sha256 is of the canonical JSON body (JSON.stringify of the file without `header`). Hand-transcribed from the fetched source documents; sha256 (when filled) is of the canonical body. Brackets, standard deductions and dependent exemption are from the Department of Revenue release of 2025-12-16 (2026 brackets, +2.369% chained-CPI adjustment); other indexed amounts are from 'Tax Year 2026 Inflation-Adjusted Amounts in Minnesota Statutes' (https://www.revenue.state.mn.us/sites/default/files/2025-12/inflation-adjusted-amounts-2026.pdf); cross-checked against Tax Foundation 2026. Starting point is federal AGI. No personal exemption for filer/spouse; the dependent exemption is $5,300 per dependent (disallowed above indexed AGI thresholds). Additional standard deduction for age 65+ or blind: $1,600 per married filer/surviving spouse, $2,000 if single or HOH (seniorExtraDeduction uses the married amount). The standard (and itemized) deduction is reduced for AGI above $244,400 ($122,200 MFS), with a second phase-out threshold at $337,800 ($168,900 MFS) and the maximum 80% reduction above $1,107,750. Social Security is PARTIALLY taxed: under the simplified method all federally taxable benefits are subtracted when AGI is at or below $110,780 (MFJ/surviving spouse), $86,410 (single/HOH) or $55,390 (MFS); above that the subtraction is reduced 10% for each $4,000 of AGI over the threshold ($2,000 for MFS), so it is gone $40,000 ($20,000 MFS) above the threshold; an alternative provisional-income method (maximum subtraction $5,840 MFJ / $4,560 single-HOH / $2,920 MFS) may be used if larger. No general pension/IRA exclusion; a public-pension subtraction of up to $13,850 (single/HOH/MFS) or $27,690 (MFJ) for qualifying government pensions phases out above the same AGI thresholds. Special regimes not modeled: Minnesota's 1% net investment income tax on net investment income over $1,000,000; Minnesota AMT; child and working family credits. Brackets, standard deduction and exemption are indexed annually (chained CPI-U).
